ex:Report.aristotelian_definition: A Report is an InformationContentEntity that records structured information about technology development, trends, value chains and markets.

ex:TechnologyDevelopmentStatusReport.aristotelian_definition: A TechnologyDevelopmentStatusReport is an InformationContentEntity that documents the status and trends of technology development, including readiness levels, deployment, costs, funding, patenting, and scientific publication.

ex:WindEnergyTechnology.aristotelian_definition: A WindEnergyTechnology is a MaterialEntity that represents the technology used for generating electricity from wind energy.

ex:CETOProject.comment: Covers objectives and contributions from colleagues.
ex:CETOProject.aristotelian_definition: A project that monitors EU research and innovation activities on clean energy technologies, assesses the competitiveness of the EU clean energy sector, builds on existing Commission studies, and publishes reports.

ex:AnnualProgressReport.comment: Documents annual progress in clean energy technology.
ex:AnnualProgressReport.aristotelian_definition: A report published annually by the Commission on the competitiveness of clean energy technologies, serving as a primary source of data.

ex:RenewableEnergyShareTarget.aristotelian_definition: A target set by the EU for its renewable energy share, aiming to reach at least 42.5% of final energy consumption by 2030.

ex:OnshoreWindCostReduction.aristotelian_definition: The process of reducing the cost of onshore wind between 2010 and 2022, resulting in a levelised cost of energy (LCoE) of EUR 31 per MWh.

ex:GlobalMarketShare.aristotelian_definition: The share of the global wind turbine market held by Chinese, European, and North American OEMs as of 2023.

ex:EURDFrameworkProgrammeInvestment.aristotelian_definition: The investment in wind energy research and development by the EU framework programmes, including Horizon 2020 and Horizon Europe.

ex:PrivateRDInvestment.comment: Covers the investment percentage from 2010 to 2020.
ex:PrivateRDInvestment.aristotelian_definition: The process of private research and development funding invested in various technologies, particularly focusing on wind energy.

ex:SWOTAnalysis.comment: Maps to CETO SWOT analysis for the competitiveness of the EU wind energy sector.
ex:SWOTAnalysis.aristotelian_definition: A structured analysis of strengths, weaknesses, opportunities, and threats related to the competitiveness of the EU wind energy sector.

ex:TechnologyReadinessLevel.comment: Covers the current TRL of onshore and bottom-fixed offshore wind turbines.
ex:TechnologyReadinessLevel.aristotelian_definition: The stage of technological development, indicating how close a technology is to commercialization.

ex:FloatingOffshoreWindSubstructure.comment: Includes types like Spar-buoy, Semi-Submersible, TLP, Barge, and Multi-Platforms.
ex:FloatingOffshoreWindSubstructure.aristotelian_definition: The substructures used in floating offshore wind technology to provide buoyancy and stability.

ex:PreCommercialFloatingOffshoreWindDesi.comment: Includes designs like Spar-buoy and Semi-Submersible in the North Sea and Atlantic Ocean.
ex:PreCommercialFloatingOffshoreWindDesi.aristotelian_definition: The design of floating offshore wind technology that has been deployed pre-commercially.

ex:LowerTRLTechnology.comment: Includes technologies like Airborne Wind Energy Systems (AWES) and Vertical Axis Wind Turbines (VAWT).
ex:LowerTRLTechnology.aristotelian_definition: Technologies generating electricity that are at a lower technology readiness level than onshore and bottom-fixed offshore wind turbines.

ex:AirborneWindEnergySystem.comment: Airborne wind energy systems are at a lower TRL than other wind technologies.
ex:AirborneWindEnergySystem.aristotelian_definition: A technology that converts wind energy into electricity using autonomous kites or unmanned aircrafts, linked to the ground by one or more tethers.

ex:VerticalAxisWindTurbine.comment: Vertical axis wind turbines are less efficient than conventional horizontal axis wind turbines.
ex:VerticalAxisWindTurbine.aristotelian_definition: A type of wind turbine that uses a vertical shaft around which the rotor turns, offering lower efficiency compared to horizontal axis wind turbines but potentially gaining momentum through hybridization or small-scale applications.

ex:OnshoreWindInstalledCapacity2030.comment: This class represents a specific projection for onshore wind energy.
ex:OnshoreWindInstalledCapacity2030.aristotelian_definition: The projected installed capacity of onshore wind in the EU by 2030 under the POTEnCIA CETO 2024 scenario.

ex:OnshoreWindInstalledCapacity2050.comment: This class represents a specific projection for onshore wind energy.
ex:OnshoreWindInstalledCapacity2050.aristotelian_definition: The projected installed capacity of onshore wind in the EU by 2050 under the POTEnCIA CETO 2024 scenario.

ex:OffshoreWindInstalledCapacity2030.comment: This class represents a specific projection for offshore wind energy.
ex:OffshoreWindInstalledCapacity2030.aristotelian_definition: The projected installed capacity of offshore wind in the EU by 2030 under the POTEnCIA CETO 2024 scenario.

ex:OffshoreWindInstalledCapacity2050.comment: This class represents a specific projection for offshore wind energy.
ex:OffshoreWindInstalledCapacity2050.aristotelian_definition: The projected installed capacity of offshore wind in the EU by 2050 under the POTEnCIA CETO 2024 scenario.

ex:GlobalWindEnergyInstalledCapacity2030.comment: This class represents a specific projection for global wind energy.
ex:GlobalWindEnergyInstalledCapacity2030.aristotelian_definition: The projected installed capacity of global wind energy by 2030 under the Global CETO 2°C scenario 2024.

ex:GlobalWindEnergyInstalledCapacity2050.comment: This class represents a specific projection for global wind energy.
ex:GlobalWindEnergyInstalledCapacity2050.aristotelian_definition: The projected installed capacity of global wind energy by 2050 under the Global CETO 2°C scenario 2024.

http://example.org/vc_pe_investment_stag.comment: This class is used to categorize different stages of VC/PE investment.
http://example.org/vc_pe_investment_stag.aristotelian_definition: A classification of venture capital and private equity investments based on the stage of development of the investee company.

ex:InvestmentDealStage.comment: A classification of venture capital and private equity investments based on the stage of development of the investee company.
ex:InvestmentDealStage.aristotelian_definition: An InvestmentDealStage is a Quality that categorizes venture capital and private equity investments based on the developmental phase of the company receiving the investment.

ex:WindEnergyInvestment.comment: Venture capital and private equity investment in the wind energy sector.
ex:WindEnergyInvestment.aristotelian_definition: A WindEnergyInvestment is a Process that represents the financial commitment of venture capital and private equity into the wind energy sector.

ex:WindEnergyInvention.comment: A novel creation or discovery in the wind energy sector, represented by patent families.
ex:WindEnergyInvention.aristotelian_definition: A WindEnergyInvention is a MaterialEntity that represents a novel creation or discovery within the field of wind energy, often protected by patent families.

ex:HighValueInvention.comment: A wind energy invention considered high-value due to patent applications filed in more than one patent office.
ex:HighValueInvention.aristotelian_definition: A HighValueInvention is a WindEnergyInvention that is considered significant due to its broad protection across multiple patent offices, indicating substantial commercial or technological importance.

ex:InternationalInvention.comment: A wind energy invention for which patent applications are protected in a country other than the applicant's residence.
ex:InternationalInvention.aristotelian_definition: An InternationalInvention is a WindEnergyInvention where the patent application is protected in a country other than the applicant's residence, signifying cross-border intellectual property protection.

ex:CooperativePatentClassificationCode.comment: A standardized code used for evaluating patenting activity in the wind sector.
ex:CooperativePatentClassificationCode.aristotelian_definition: A CooperativePatentClassificationCode is an InformationContentEntity that serves as a standardized code used to categorize and evaluate patenting activity within a specific technological domain.

ex:WindEnergyPublication.comment: A peer-reviewed article or scholarly work related to the wind energy sector.
ex:WindEnergyPublication.aristotelian_definition: A WindEnergyPublication is an InformationContentEntity that represents a peer-reviewed article or other scholarly work discussing research and findings in the field of wind energy.

ex:HighlyCitedPublication.comment: A wind energy publication that is among the top 10% most cited papers in its field and year.
ex:HighlyCitedPublication.aristotelian_definition: A HighlyCitedPublication is a WindEnergyPublication that belongs to the top 10% most cited papers within its field and year, indicating significant impact and recognition.

ex:CountryPublicationImpact.comment: A measure of the citation impact of publications from a country compared to the global average in the research field.
ex:CountryPublicationImpact.aristotelian_definition: A CountryPublicationImpact is a Quality that measures the citation impact of publications from a specific country relative to the global average for that research field.

ex:CountryPublicationProductivity.comment: A measure of both the productivity and citation impact of publications from a country.
ex:CountryPublicationProductivity.aristotelian_definition: A CountryPublicationProductivity is a Quality that assesses both the output (productivity) and the citation impact (h-index) of publications originating from a specific country.

ex:OriginalEquipmentManufacturer.comment: A company that manufactures and sells equipment, often in the wind energy sector, under its own brand.
ex:OriginalEquipmentManufacturer.aristotelian_definition: An OriginalEquipmentManufacturer is a Role that designs, manufactures, and sells equipment under its own brand name, particularly in the context of the wind energy sector.

ex:CountryPublicationActivity.comment: Represents the number of peer-reviewed articles published by a country in wind energy research.
ex:CountryPublicationActivity.aristotelian_definition: A CountryPublicationActivity is an InformationContentEntity that represents the scholarly output of a specific country in the field of wind energy research, measured by the number of peer-reviewed articles published within a defined period.

ex:CollaborationNetwork.comment: Describes the co-publication relationships between entities in a research domain.
ex:CollaborationNetwork.aristotelian_definition: A CollaborationNetwork is an InformationContentEntity that visualizes and describes the co-publication relationships between different entities (e.g., countries, organizations) in a specific research domain.

ex:WindEnergyResearchProject.comment: Represents a funded initiative or program in wind energy research and innovation.
ex:WindEnergyResearchProject.aristotelian_definition: A WindEnergyResearchProject is an InformationContentEntity that represents a funded initiative or program focused on advancing research and innovation within the wind energy sector.

ex:RecyclingCircularityProject.comment: A wind energy research project focused on recycling and circularity solutions.
ex:RecyclingCircularityProject.aristotelian_definition: A RecyclingCircularityProject is a WindEnergyResearchProject that specifically focuses on developing solutions for recycling and promoting circular economy principles within the wind energy sector, particularly concerning end-of-life components.

ex:BladeRecyclingProject.comment: A project focused on developing recycling solutions for wind turbine blades.
ex:BladeRecyclingProject.aristotelian_definition: A BladeRecyclingProject is a RecyclingCircularityProject that aims to develop and implement recycling solutions for wind turbine blades.

ex:GridIntegrationProject.comment: A wind energy research project focused on improving grid integration.
ex:GridIntegrationProject.aristotelian_definition: A GridIntegrationProject is a WindEnergyResearchProject that focuses on improving the integration of wind energy into existing power grids, including aspects like converter interoperability and smart curtailment.

ex:ConverterInteroperabilityProject.comment: A project focused on improving the interoperability of converters for grid integration.
ex:ConverterInteroperabilityProject.aristotelian_definition: A ConverterInteroperabilityProject is a GridIntegrationProject that aims to enhance the grid-forming capabilities and interoperability of offshore and onshore converters within high-voltage direct current systems.

ex:FloatingOffshoreWindProject.comment: A wind energy research project focused on floating offshore wind technology.
ex:FloatingOffshoreWindProject.aristotelian_definition: A FloatingOffshoreWindProject is a WindEnergyResearchProject that focuses on the development, demonstration, or industrialization of floating offshore wind technologies.

ex:BatterySupplyChainProject.comment: A project focused on establishing a sustainable supply chain for lithium-ion batteries used in renewable energy.
ex:BatterySupplyChainProject.aristotelian_definition: A BatterySupplyChainProject is a WindEnergyResearchProject that aims to establish a sustainable end-to-end supply chain for lithium-ion batteries, particularly for applications in electric vehicles and renewable energy sources like solar and wind farms.

http://example.org/TWAIN.comment: Priority: Maintenance and condition monitoring systems
http://example.org/TWAIN.aristotelian_definition: A project focusing on the efficient deployment of AI in wind farm control and asset management to optimize operation for cost, performance, and efficiency while considering environmental and societal aspects.

http://example.org/ULTFARMS.comment: Priority: Environmental impacts of wind energy
http://example.org/ULTFARMS.aristotelian_definition: A project developing novel designs in six low trophic aquaculture pilots in offshore wind farm locations across the North and Baltic Seas to understand environmental impacts.

http://example.org/off-coustics.comment: Priority: Environmental impacts of wind energy
http://example.org/off-coustics.aristotelian_definition: A project aiming to achieve a comprehensive understanding of the acoustic repercussions of wind turbines, specifically their potential negative impact on marine life through acoustic damage.

http://example.org/FLOW.aristotelian_definition: A project developing new prediction methods for production statistics and load performance of modern GW-scale and 400-metre tall offshore and onshore wind energy systems.

http://example.org/MADE4WIND.aristotelian_definition: A project developing and testing innovative components for a 15 MW floating wind turbine, including new designs and manufacturing techniques in lightweight materials, recyclability, and advanced software tools.

http://example.org/Nanowings.aristotelian_definition: A project improving wind turbine performance and durability by developing nanocoating based on a blended formulation of super-glue polymers combined with nanoparticles, providing outstanding anti-icing and anti-fouling properties.

http://example.org/WIMBY.aristotelian_definition: A project studying the drivers and barriers of social acceptance to address related challenges, gaining more popular support for wind energy.

http://example.org/DATA-DRIVEN OFFSHORE.aristotelian_definition: A project revolutionizing aerohydroelastic simulations used in wind turbine research and development by integrating experimental data into these simulations.

http://example.org/Orcelle.aristotelian_definition: A project developing a solution involving wind as the main form of propulsion, aiming for an energy efficiency gain of more than 50%.

http://example.org/WHISPER.aristotelian_definition: A project developing a modular retrofit solution, including a wingsail system for wind-assisted propulsion and testing efficiency savings of more than 20%.

http://example.org/i4Offshore.aristotelian_definition: A project aiming to reduce cost barriers in large-scale offshore developments by optimizing low-cost manufacturing through a hybrid-material gravity jacket foundation.

http://example.org/COREWIND.aristotelian_definition: A project contributing to cost and environmental footprint reductions in floating offshore wind energy systems by using digital tools and optimizing designs for station-keeping systems and dynamic cables.

http://example.org/SUSMAGPRO.aristotelian_definition: A project focusing on recycling and reusing neodymium-containing magnets from waste, creating a shorter recycling loop with higher recovery rate and increased yield.

http://example.org/NAWEP.aristotelian_definition: A project aiming to construct and operate an onshore array of at least twelve 100 kW AWES devices, generating a combined 1.2 MW with targeted cost and carbon footprint reductions.

http://example.org/Aquilon.aristotelian_definition: A project serving as a demonstrator for airborne wind energy production at 160 kW scale and an integrated renewable energy and storage solution.

http://example.org/N2OWF.aristotelian_definition: A project building and operating a first-of-its-kind offshore wind farm with 450 MW capacity, combined with on-site production, storage, and offtake of green hydrogen.

http://example.org/SUSTAIN-SEA.aristotelian_definition: A project using wind energy to reduce fuel use and GHG emissions in the maritime transport sector by integrating a wind propulsion system into five large cargo vessels.

http://example.org/HIPPOW.aristotelian_definition: A project aiming to build and operate a 15 MW floating wind turbine with innovative technologies including wind turbines, foundations, and hydrogen technology solutions.

http://example.org/SEAWORTHY.aristotelian_definition: A project building and operating a 15 MW floating wind turbine with innovative technologies including wind turbines, foundations, and hydrogen technology solutions.

http://example.org/hippow_project.comment: HIPPOW project is described as a commercial-scale demonstration integrating various renewable energy sources.
http://example.org/hippow_project.aristotelian_definition: A commercial-scale demonstration of a technology capable of supplying clean dispatchable offshore power from wind, waves and hydrogen.

http://example.org/seaworthy_project.comment: SEAWORTHY project is described as a commercial-scale demonstration integrating various renewable energy sources.
http://example.org/seaworthy_project.aristotelian_definition: A commercial-scale demonstration of technology capable of supplying clean dispatchable offshore power from wind, waves and hydrogen.

http://example.org/wind_energy_trade.comment: This class captures the overall context of international trade in wind generating sets.
http://example.org/wind_energy_trade.aristotelian_definition: The exchange and flow of wind generating sets between different countries, particularly focusing on the EU's trade dynamics.

http://example.org/import_export_ratio.comment: This class represents the quantitative relationship between imports and exports.
http://example.org/import_export_ratio.aristotelian_definition: The ratio between extra-EU imports and exports, indicating market share dynamics.

http://example.org/critical_raw_material.comment: This class describes the supply chain for essential components of wind turbines.
http://example.org/critical_raw_material.aristotelian_definition: The entire process from extraction to manufacturing of critical raw materials used in wind power plants, particularly focusing on rare earth elements and permanent magnets.

http://example.org/balsa_wood.comment: This class defines the specific material balsa wood and its usage.
http://example.org/balsa_wood.aristotelian_definition: A lightweight, stiff material used in wind turbine blades, especially in spar caps and blade cores.

http://example.org/material_intensity.comment: This class quantifies the material requirements for wind turbine construction.
http://example.org/material_intensity.aristotelian_definition: The amount of raw or composite materials required per unit of installed capacity in wind turbines.

http://www.w3.org/2002/07/owl#Class.comment: These are essential for the production of permanent magnets in turbine generators.
http://www.w3.org/2002/07/owl#Class.aristotelian_definition: Critical raw materials used in wind energy technology, specifically Neodymium magnets.

http://example.org/new_knowledge.comment: This class represents the newly generated knowledge based on the references provided.
http://example.org/new_knowledge.aristotelian_definition: A new piece of information derived from existing sources.

http://example.org/report_on_socio_econo.comment: Describes the socio-economic impacts of community wind power projects in Northern Scotland.
http://example.org/report_on_socio_econo.aristotelian_definition: A report published by an organization on the socio-economic impacts of community wind power projects in Northern Scotland.

http://example.org/report_on_socio_econo.comment: Describes the socio-economic impact of offshore wind projects.
http://example.org/report_on_socio_econo.aristotelian_definition: A report published by an organization on the socio-economic impact study of offshore wind.

http://example.org/jrc_idees_2021_databa.comment: Provides updates and documentation for the JRC's energy system database.
http://example.org/jrc_idees_2021_databa.aristotelian_definition: Technical documentation and database update for the Integrated Database of the European Energy System by the JRC.

http://example.org/wind_energy_technolog.comment: Reports on the technology development, trends, value chains, and markets of wind energy in the EU.
http://example.org/wind_energy_technolog.aristotelian_definition: A report published by the Clean Energy Technology Observatory on wind energy in the European Union.

http://example.org/report_on_potencia_ce.comment: Describes the scenario for the EU energy outlook to 2050 under the POTEnCIA framework.
http://example.org/report_on_potencia_ce.aristotelian_definition: A report published by an organization on the POTEnCIA CETO 2024 scenario for EU energy outlook to 2050.

ex:OffshoreWindCapacityAddition.comment: Represents the annual or periodic increase in installed offshore wind power capacity.
ex:OffshoreWindCapacityAddition.aristotelian_definition: An OffshoreWindCapacityAddition is a Process that represents the addition of new offshore wind power generation capacity over a specific period.

ex:OnshoreWindCapacityAddition.comment: Represents the annual or periodic increase in installed onshore wind power capacity.
ex:OnshoreWindCapacityAddition.aristotelian_definition: An OnshoreWindCapacityAddition is a Process that represents the addition of new onshore wind power generation capacity over a specific period.

ex:OffshoreWindInstalledCapacity.comment: Represents the total cumulative installed capacity of offshore wind power generation.
ex:OffshoreWindInstalledCapacity.aristotelian_definition: An OffshoreWindInstalledCapacity is a MaterialEntity that represents the total cumulative installed capacity of offshore wind power generation at a specific point in time.

ex:OnshoreWindInstalledCapacity.comment: Represents the total cumulative installed capacity of onshore wind power generation.
ex:OnshoreWindInstalledCapacity.aristotelian_definition: An OnshoreWindInstalledCapacity is a MaterialEntity that represents the total cumulative installed capacity of onshore wind power generation at a specific point in time.

ex:WindEnergyGeneration.comment: Represents the electricity generated by wind power.
ex:WindEnergyGeneration.aristotelian_definition: A WindEnergyGeneration is a Process that represents the production of electricity from wind energy over a specific period.

ex:WindEnergyLCOE.comment: Represents the Levelized Cost of Energy for wind power.
ex:WindEnergyLCOE.aristotelian_definition: A WindEnergyLCOE is a Quality that represents the Levelized Cost of Energy for wind power, indicating the average revenue per unit of electricity generation needed to recover costs of building and operating a wind power plant.

ex:WindEnergyInvestmentCost.comment: Represents the overnight investment costs for wind energy installations.
ex:WindEnergyInvestmentCost.aristotelian_definition: A WindEnergyInvestmentCost is a Quality that represents the initial capital expenditure required for building wind energy installations.

ex:PublicRAndIInvestmentWindEnergy.comment: Represents public investment in research and development for wind energy.
ex:PublicRAndIInvestmentWindEnergy.aristotelian_definition: A PublicRAndIInvestmentWindEnergy is a Process that represents public funding allocated to research and innovation activities within the wind energy sector.

ex:PrivateRAndIInvestmentWindEnergy.comment: Represents private investment in research and development for wind energy.
ex:PrivateRAndIInvestmentWindEnergy.aristotelian_definition: A PrivateRAndIInvestmentWindEnergy is a Process that represents private funding allocated to research and innovation activities within the wind energy sector.

ex:WindEnergyVCPEInvestment.comment: Represents venture capital and private equity investment in the wind energy sector.
ex:WindEnergyVCPEInvestment.aristotelian_definition: A WindEnergyVCPEInvestment is a Process that represents financial investment by venture capital and private equity firms into the wind energy sector.

ex:WindEnergyInventionActivity.comment: Represents the activity of inventing within the wind energy sector.
ex:WindEnergyInventionActivity.aristotelian_definition: A WindEnergyInventionActivity is a Process that represents the creation and documentation of new inventions within the wind energy sector.

ex:WindEnergyPublicationActivity.comment: Represents the activity of publishing research in the wind energy sector.
ex:WindEnergyPublicationActivity.aristotelian_definition: A WindEnergyPublicationActivity is a Process that represents the creation and dissemination of peer-reviewed articles and scholarly works in the field of wind energy.

ex:WindEnergyFundingEvolution.comment: Represents the evolution of funding for wind energy research and innovation.
ex:WindEnergyFundingEvolution.aristotelian_definition: A WindEnergyFundingEvolution is a Process that tracks the changes and trends in research and innovation funding for wind energy over time.

ex:WindSectorTurnover.comment: Represents the turnover of the wind energy sector.
ex:WindSectorTurnover.aristotelian_definition: A WindSectorTurnover is a Process that represents the total revenue generated by the wind energy sector over a specific period.

ex:WindSectorGVA.comment: Represents the Gross Value Added of the wind energy sector.
ex:WindSectorGVA.aristotelian_definition: A WindSectorGVA is a Process that represents the Gross Value Added generated by the wind energy sector, indicating its contribution to the economy.

ex:WindTurbineMarketShare.comment: Represents the market share of wind turbines.
ex:WindTurbineMarketShare.aristotelian_definition: A WindTurbineMarketShare is a Quality that represents the proportion of the global or regional market for wind turbines held by specific manufacturers or regions.

ex:WindEnergyEmployment.comment: Represents the evolution of direct and indirect jobs in the wind energy sector.
ex:WindEnergyEmployment.aristotelian_definition: A WindEnergyEmployment is a Process that represents the number of direct and indirect jobs within the wind energy sector over a specific period.

ex:RawMaterial.comment: Represents the basic substances used in the production of wind power plants.
ex:RawMaterial.aristotelian_definition: A RawMaterial is a MaterialEntity that is a basic substance in its natural or processed state, used as a component in the manufacturing of wind power plants.

ex:MaterialIntensity.comment: Measures the material consumption per unit of wind turbine capacity.
ex:MaterialIntensity.aristotelian_definition: A MaterialIntensity is a Quality that quantifies the amount of raw or composite materials required per unit of installed capacity in wind turbines.

ex:WindTurbineType.comment: Represents a specific classification or design of a wind turbine.
ex:WindTurbineType.aristotelian_definition: A WindTurbineType is a MaterialEntity that represents a specific category or design of wind turbine used for generating electricity from wind energy.

ex:RareEarthElement.comment: Represents rare earth elements used in wind turbine components, particularly magnets.
ex:RareEarthElement.aristotelian_definition: A RareEarthElement is a RawMaterial that is a group of 17 chemically similar metallic elements with unique properties crucial for various high-tech applications, including wind turbine magnets.

ex:PermanentMagnet.comment: Represents magnetic materials used in wind turbine generators.
ex:PermanentMagnet.aristotelian_definition: A PermanentMagnet is a RawMaterial that is a magnetic material that retains its magnetism after being magnetized, commonly used in wind turbine generators.

ex:OnshoreWindTurbine.comment: Represents a wind turbine installed on land.
ex:OnshoreWindTurbine.aristotelian_definition: An OnshoreWindTurbine is a WindTurbineType that is designed and installed for generating electricity from wind on land.

ex:OffshoreWindTurbine.comment: Represents a wind turbine installed offshore.
ex:OffshoreWindTurbine.aristotelian_definition: An OffshoreWindTurbine is a WindTurbineType that is designed and installed for generating electricity from wind in bodies of water.

ex:GHGEmissions.comment: Quantifies greenhouse gas emissions associated with wind energy generation.
ex:GHGEmissions.aristotelian_definition: A GHGEmissions is a Quality that quantifies the amount of greenhouse gases released into the atmosphere per unit of energy produced by wind power plants.

ex:EnergyPaybackTime.comment: Measures the time it takes for a wind energy system to repay its energy investment.
ex:EnergyPaybackTime.aristotelian_definition: An EnergyPaybackTime is a Quality that represents the time required for a wind energy system to generate the amount of energy equivalent to the energy consumed during its entire lifecycle.

ex:BenthicBiodiversity.comment: Refers to the biodiversity found on the bottom of marine or freshwater ecosystems.
ex:BenthicBiodiversity.aristotelian_definition: A BenthicBiodiversity is a MaterialEntity that represents the variety of life forms and their ecological interactions within the seabed environment.

ex:SeabedRecovery.comment: The process by which the seabed ecosystem recovers from disturbances or pressures.
ex:SeabedRecovery.aristotelian_definition: A SeabedRecovery is a Process that describes the natural regeneration and restoration of the seabed ecosystem, potentially facilitated by reduced human activity.

ex:BenthicFaunalBaseline.comment: A foundational dataset describing the state of benthic fauna before significant development or change.
ex:BenthicFaunalBaseline.aristotelian_definition: A BenthicFaunalBaseline is an InformationContentEntity that serves as a reference point for the composition and abundance of benthic fauna against which future changes can be assessed.

ex:BlueWaterConsumption.comment: Measures the freshwater footprint of an activity or product.
ex:BlueWaterConsumption.aristotelian_definition: A BlueWaterConsumption is a Quality that quantifies the net balance of freshwater inputs and outputs throughout the lifecycle of a product or process.

ex:WaterScarcityFootprint.comment: Quantifies the contribution to water scarcity based on available water remaining.
ex:WaterScarcityFootprint.aristotelian_definition: A WaterScarcityFootprint is a Quality that assesses the impact of water consumption on water availability in a specific region, using a defined methodology like AWARE.

ex:NdFeBMagnetProduction.comment: The industrial process of manufacturing NdFeB permanent magnets.
ex:NdFeBMagnetProduction.aristotelian_definition: A NdFeBMagnetProduction is a Process that encompasses the manufacturing steps involved in creating Neodymium-Iron-Boron permanent magnets.

ex:ResourceDepletionWater.comment: Quantifies water used in resource extraction and processing that leads to depletion.
ex:ResourceDepletionWater.aristotelian_definition: A ResourceDepletionWater is a Quality that measures the volume of water consumed during the extraction and processing of resources, contributing to water depletion.

ex:HumanToxicityPotential.comment: An environmental impact category assessing health effects from toxic substances.
ex:HumanToxicityPotential.aristotelian_definition: A HumanToxicityPotential is a Quality that measures the potential impact on human health from toxic substances released into the environment.

ex:InstalledPowerDensity.comment: Measures the power output relative to the land or sea area occupied.
ex:InstalledPowerDensity.aristotelian_definition: An InstalledPowerDensity is a Quality that represents the amount of power generation capacity installed per unit of area.

ex:SoilAcidificationPotential.comment: An environmental impact category measuring the potential for soil acidification.
ex:SoilAcidificationPotential.aristotelian_definition: A SoilAcidificationPotential is a Quality that quantifies the potential for substances released during a process to cause acidification of the soil.

ex:SoilEutrophicationPotential.comment: An environmental impact category measuring the potential for soil eutrophication.
ex:SoilEutrophicationPotential.aristotelian_definition: A SoilEutrophicationPotential is a Quality that quantifies the potential for substances released during a process to cause excessive nutrient enrichment in the soil.

ex:SoilPollution.comment: Contamination of soil by harmful substances.
ex:SoilPollution.aristotelian_definition: A SoilPollution is a Quality that describes the presence of contaminants in the soil that can be harmful to the environment or human health.

ex:HazardousMaterial.comment: Substances that pose a risk due to their properties.
ex:HazardousMaterial.aristotelian_definition: A HazardousMaterial is a MaterialEntity that possesses properties that make it capable of causing harm to human health or the environment.

ex:EconomicLCCStandard.comment: A standard or best practice for evaluating the total cost of ownership over a product's or project's lifecycle.
ex:EconomicLCCStandard.aristotelian_definition: An EconomicLCCStandard is an InformationContentEntity that defines best practices or methodologies for assessing the life cycle cost of economic activities or projects.

ex:CriticalRawMaterial.comment: Raw materials vital for technology with a high risk of supply shortage.
ex:CriticalRawMaterial.aristotelian_definition: A CriticalRawMaterial is a MaterialEntity that is essential for technological applications but faces a high risk of supply disruption.

ex:CompositeWaste.comment: Waste material derived from composite structures, particularly wind turbine blades.
ex:CompositeWaste.aristotelian_definition: A CompositeWaste is a MaterialEntity that consists of discarded materials made from a combination of different components, such as those found in wind turbine blades.

ex:RecyclingInfrastructure.comment: The physical setup and resources required for recycling processes.
ex:RecyclingInfrastructure.aristotelian_definition: A RecyclingInfrastructure is a MaterialEntity that comprises the facilities, equipment, and systems necessary for processing waste materials for reuse or recovery.

ex:PermittingProcess.comment: The sequence of steps and regulations involved in obtaining official permission for a project.
ex:PermittingProcess.aristotelian_definition: A PermittingProcess is a Process that involves the procedures and requirements for obtaining official authorization to undertake a specific activity or project, such as constructing a wind farm.

ex:OneStopShopPermittingModel.comment: An administrative model that consolidates all permitting procedures into a single entity.
ex:OneStopShopPermittingModel.aristotelian_definition: A OneStopShopPermittingModel is a Process that centralizes all necessary administrative and regulatory steps for project permitting through a single point of contact or agency.

ex:LowFrequencyNoise.comment: Sound characterized by low frequencies, often associated with wind turbine operation.
ex:LowFrequencyNoise.aristotelian_definition: A LowFrequencyNoise is a Quality that refers to sound waves with frequencies typically below 200 Hz, which can be emitted by wind turbines.

ex:PsychoMedicalEffect.comment: Adverse psychological or physiological responses to environmental factors.
ex:PsychoMedicalEffect.aristotelian_definition: A PsychoMedicalEffect is a Quality that describes the psychological or medical symptoms experienced by individuals due to exposure to certain stimuli, such as noise.

ex:DirectPhysicalEffect.comment: A tangible, measurable physical impact on the body.
ex:DirectPhysicalEffect.aristotelian_definition: A DirectPhysicalEffect is a Quality that denotes a physiological impact on the human body directly caused by an external factor, independent of psychological perception.

ex:ResidentAttitude.comment: The perspective or stance of local residents towards wind energy installations.
ex:ResidentAttitude.aristotelian_definition: A ResidentAttitude is a Quality that represents the disposition, feelings, or opinions held by individuals living in proximity to wind turbines regarding their presence and impact.

ex:ExposureSymptom.comment: Represents reported symptoms resulting from exposure to environmental factors like wind turbine noise.
ex:ExposureSymptom.aristotelian_definition: An ExposureSymptom is a Quality that describes a physical or psychological manifestation reported by individuals due to exposure to a specific factor, such as infrasound and low frequency noise from wind turbines.

ex:LowFrequencyNoiseEffect.comment: Describes the potential health or perceptual effects associated with low-frequency noise from wind turbines.
ex:LowFrequencyNoiseEffect.aristotelian_definition: A LowFrequencyNoiseEffect is a Quality that describes a potential impact on human health or perception resulting from exposure to low-frequency noise, particularly from wind turbines, for which scientific understanding may be limited.

ex:InfrasoundEffect.comment: Describes the potential health or perceptual effects associated with infrasound from wind turbines.
ex:InfrasoundEffect.aristotelian_definition: An InfrasoundEffect is a Quality that describes a potential impact on human health or perception resulting from exposure to infrasound, particularly from wind turbines, for which scientific understanding may be limited.

ex:WindTurbineNoisePerception.comment: Refers to the subjective interpretation and experience of noise from wind turbines.
ex:WindTurbineNoisePerception.aristotelian_definition: A WindTurbineNoisePerception is a Quality that represents how individuals perceive and interpret noise generated by wind turbines, which can be influenced by various factors beyond objective sound levels.

ex:SleepDisturbance.comment: Represents a disruption in normal sleep patterns, potentially linked to environmental factors.
ex:SleepDisturbance.aristotelian_definition: A SleepDisturbance is a Quality that describes an alteration or disruption in normal sleep patterns, which can be self-reported and potentially associated with environmental factors like noise.

ex:ElectromagneticFieldExposure.comment: Quantifies exposure to electromagnetic fields generated by wind turbines.
ex:ElectromagneticFieldExposure.aristotelian_definition: An ElectromagneticFieldExposure is a Quality that quantifies the level of electromagnetic fields to which individuals or the environment are subjected, particularly in the context of wind turbine operation.

ex:ShadowFlickerImpact.comment: Describes the impact on residents due to the periodic shadows cast by wind turbine rotors.
ex:ShadowFlickerImpact.aristotelian_definition: A ShadowFlickerImpact is a Quality that describes the effect on residents caused by the periodic casting of shadows from wind turbine rotors onto surrounding buildings during sunny intervals.

ex:ShadowFlickerProtectionSystem.comment: A system used in wind turbines to prevent shadow flicker impacts on residents.
ex:ShadowFlickerProtectionSystem.aristotelian_definition: A ShadowFlickerProtectionSystem is a WindEnergyTechnology that is integrated into the control system of a wind turbine to prevent or mitigate the impact of shadow flicker on surrounding areas.

ex:PublicAcceptanceDriver.comment: Factors that influence public acceptance or opposition to wind energy projects.
ex:PublicAcceptanceDriver.aristotelian_definition: A PublicAcceptanceDriver is a Quality that represents a factor influencing the level of public acceptance or opposition towards wind energy projects.

ex:RepoweringDriver.comment: Factors that drive decisions for wind energy repowering projects.
ex:RepoweringDriver.aristotelian_definition: A RepoweringDriver is a Quality that represents a factor motivating or influencing decisions related to the repowering of existing wind energy projects.

ex:LandscapeImpact.comment: The effect of wind energy projects on the visual landscape.
ex:LandscapeImpact.aristotelian_definition: A LandscapeImpact is a Quality that describes the effect of wind energy projects, particularly repowering, on the visual and aesthetic characteristics of the surrounding landscape.

ex:POTENCIAModel.comment: The Policy Oriented Tool for Energy and Climate Change Impact Assessment (POTEnCIA) model used for EU energy system analysis.
ex:POTENCIAModel.aristotelian_definition: A POTENCIAModel is an InformationContentEntity that is an energy system simulation model designed to compare alternative pathways for the EU energy system, covering energy supply and all energy demand sectors.

ex:EnergySystemSimulationModel.comment: A model used to simulate energy systems and their responses to different policies and conditions.
ex:EnergySystemSimulationModel.aristotelian_definition: An EnergySystemSimulationModel is an InformationContentEntity that is a computational model designed to simulate the behavior and interactions of energy systems under various conditions and policies.

ex:DecisionMakingSimulation.comment: Simulates the process of decision-making in energy systems, considering imperfect foresight and user behavior.
ex:DecisionMakingSimulation.aristotelian_definition: A DecisionMakingSimulation is a Process that models and replicates the process of decision-making, particularly by energy users or agents, under various constraints and policy regimes.

ex:EnergyMarketOperationSimulation.comment: Models the operation of energy markets based on economic principles and agent behavior.
ex:EnergyMarketOperationSimulation.aristotelian_definition: An EnergyMarketOperationSimulation is a Process that models the economically-driven operation of energy markets, including supply-demand interactions and the behavior of representative agents seeking to optimize their outcomes.

ex:EnergySystemHistoricalDataCalibration.comment: The process of calibrating energy system models using historical data for accurate initial conditions.
ex:EnergySystemHistoricalDataCalibration.aristotelian_definition: An EnergySystemHistoricalDataCalibration is a Process that involves adjusting the parameters and initial conditions of an energy system model using historical data to ensure accurate representation and forecasting.

ex:POTENCIACETOScenario.comment: Represents the POTEnCIA CETO 2024 scenario for EU energy system modeling.
ex:POTENCIACETOScenario.aristotelian_definition: A POTENCIACETOScenario is an InformationContentEntity that represents a climate-neutrality scenario for the EU energy system, aligning with the European Green Deal's GHG reduction objectives and incorporating policy instruments influencing technology uptake.

ex:POLESJRCModel.comment: The Prospective Outlook for the Long-term Energy System (POLES-JRC) global energy model.
ex:POLESJRCModel.aristotelian_definition: A POLESJRCModel is an EnergySystemSimulationModel that is a global energy model used to evaluate the evolution of energy demand and supply, covering primary supply, transformation, and final sectoral demand, with endogenous calculation of international markets and prices.

ex:POLESJRCModelPowerSystem.comment: Details the power system component of the POLES-JRC model.
ex:POLESJRCModelPowerSystem.aristotelian_definition: A POLESJRCModelPowerSystem is an InformationContentEntity that describes the power generation technologies, electricity demand, and power system operation and planning within the POLES-JRC model.

ex:POLESJRCModelHydrogenProduction.comment: Describes the hydrogen production routes modeled in POLES-JRC.
ex:POLESJRCModelHydrogenProduction.aristotelian_definition: A POLESJRCModelHydrogenProduction is an InformationContentEntity that outlines the various hydrogen production routes considered within the POLES-JRC model, including electrolysis, steam reforming, and gasification.

ex:POLESJRCModelBioenergy.comment: Represents the bioenergy modeling approach within the POLES-JRC model.
ex:POLESJRCModelBioenergy.aristotelian_definition: A POLESJRCModelBioenergy is an InformationContentEntity that details how bioenergy demand and supply are modeled in the POLES-JRC model, often through soft-coupling with other models like GLOBIOM-G4M.

ex:POLESJRCModelCCUS.comment: Details the integration of CCUS technologies in the POLES-JRC model.
ex:POLESJRCModelCCUS.aristotelian_definition: A POLESJRCModelCCUS is an InformationContentEntity that specifies the applications of Carbon Capture, Utilization, and Storage (CCUS) technologies within the POLES-JRC model across power generation, hydrogen production, and industrial sectors.

ex:TechnologyLearningInPOLESJRC.comment: The process of incorporating technology learning into the POLES-JRC model.
ex:TechnologyLearningInPOLESJRC.aristotelian_definition: A TechnologyLearningInPOLESJRC is a Process that describes the enhancement of the POLES-JRC model to capture technology learning effects, particularly for clean energy technologies, through methods like learning-by-doing.

ex:LearningByDoingApproach.comment: Represents the concept of cost reduction or efficiency improvement in technologies due to accumulated experience and production.
ex:LearningByDoingApproach.aristotelian_definition: A LearningByDoingApproach is a Process that models the reduction in cost or improvement in efficiency of a technology as its cumulative capacity or production increases.

ex:LearningRate.comment: A parameter within learning-by-doing models that indicates the rate of cost reduction with increased experience.
ex:LearningRate.aristotelian_definition: A LearningRate is a Quality that quantifies the percentage change in the cost of an energy technology based on a doubling of its cumulative capacity or production.

ex:FloorCost.comment: The minimum cost threshold for a component or technology, below which further cost reductions from learning are not expected.
ex:FloorCost.aristotelian_definition: A FloorCost is a Quality that specifies the minimum achievable investment cost for a component or technology, acting as a limit for cost reduction through learning.

ex:ComponentLevelLearning.comment: Applies learning-by-doing principles at the component level to capture cross-technology and cross-sectoral spillover effects.
ex:ComponentLevelLearning.aristotelian_definition: A ComponentLevelLearning is a LearningByDoingApproach that applies learning-by-doing principles to individual components of technologies, allowing for the modeling of spillover effects across different technologies and sectors.

ex:GlobalCarbonPriceScenario.comment: A scenario driven by a global carbon price trajectory to limit global warming, incorporating enacted policies but not future pledges.
ex:GlobalCarbonPriceScenario.aristotelian_definition: A GlobalCarbonPriceScenario is an InformationContentEntity that defines a pathway for limiting global temperature increase by implementing a single global carbon price across all regions, considering enacted climate policies but not long-term pledges.

ex:DecarbonisationScenario.comment: A scenario focused on achieving net greenhouse gas emission reductions aligned with climate law objectives and sector-specific legislation.
ex:DecarbonisationScenario.aristotelian_definition: A DecarbonisationScenario is an InformationContentEntity that outlines a trajectory for achieving net greenhouse gas emission reductions aligned with specific climate laws and considering sector-specific legislation.

ex:EnergySystemScenario.comment: A projection or simulation of the future energy system under specific assumptions and policy frameworks.
ex:EnergySystemScenario.aristotelian_definition: An EnergySystemScenario is an InformationContentEntity that represents a simulation or projection of the future energy system, considering various techno-economic assumptions, fuel costs, and policy incentives.

ex:TechnologyLearningEnhancement.comment: The process of enhancing energy system models to better represent endogenous learning effects in clean energy technologies.
ex:TechnologyLearningEnhancement.aristotelian_definition: A TechnologyLearningEnhancement is a Process that involves improving energy system models to better capture the effects of endogenous learning in clean energy technologies.

ex:TechnoEconomicParameterUpdate.comment: The process of revising and updating techno-economic parameters within energy system models.
ex:TechnoEconomicParameterUpdate.aristotelian_definition: A TechnoEconomicParameterUpdate is a Process that involves revising and updating the techno-economic parameters used in energy system models, often based on expert knowledge and recent data.

ex:HorizonEuropeRAndIProject.comment: A research and innovation project funded by the Horizon Europe programme related to wind energy.
ex:HorizonEuropeRAndIProject.aristotelian_definition: A HorizonEuropeRAndIProject is a WindEnergyResearchProject that is funded under the Horizon Europe programme and focuses on research and innovation within the wind energy sector.

ex:FloatingOffshoreWindProjectHorizonEur.comment: A Horizon Europe funded project focused on floating offshore wind technology.
ex:FloatingOffshoreWindProjectHorizonEur.aristotelian_definition: A FloatingOffshoreWindProjectHorizonEurope is a HorizonEuropeRAndIProject that specifically focuses on the development, demonstration, or industrialization of floating offshore wind technologies.

ex:WindEnergySocialEngagementProject.comment: A Horizon Europe funded project focused on social engagement aspects of wind energy.
ex:WindEnergySocialEngagementProject.aristotelian_definition: A WindEnergySocialEngagementProject is a HorizonEuropeRAndIProject that addresses social aspects, acceptance, or engagement related to wind energy projects.

ex:WindEnergyResourceAssessmentProject.comment: A Horizon Europe funded project focused on assessing wind energy resources.
ex:WindEnergyResourceAssessmentProject.aristotelian_definition: A WindEnergyResourceAssessmentProject is a HorizonEuropeRAndIProject that focuses on assessing and understanding the resources available for wind energy generation.

ex:WindEnergyEnvironmentalImpactProject.comment: A Horizon Europe funded project focused on the environmental impacts of wind energy.
ex:WindEnergyEnvironmentalImpactProject.aristotelian_definition: A WindEnergyEnvironmentalImpactProject is a HorizonEuropeRAndIProject that investigates the environmental impacts associated with wind energy technologies and projects.

ex:WindEnergyNewTurbineMaterialsProject.comment: A Horizon Europe funded project focused on new materials for wind turbines.
ex:WindEnergyNewTurbineMaterialsProject.aristotelian_definition: A WindEnergyNewTurbineMaterialsProject is a HorizonEuropeRAndIProject that focuses on the development and application of new materials for wind turbine components.

ex:WindEnergyMaintenanceProject.comment: A Horizon Europe funded project focused on maintenance and condition monitoring for wind energy systems.
ex:WindEnergyMaintenanceProject.aristotelian_definition: A WindEnergyMaintenanceProject is a HorizonEuropeRAndIProject that focuses on improving maintenance strategies, condition monitoring systems, or related technologies for wind energy systems.

ex:WindEnergyGridIntegrationProjectHoriz.comment: A Horizon Europe funded project focused on grid integration of wind energy.
ex:WindEnergyGridIntegrationProjectHoriz.aristotelian_definition: A WindEnergyGridIntegrationProjectHorizonEurope is a HorizonEuropeRAndIProject that focuses on enhancing the integration of wind energy into electrical grids.

http://example.org/BLOW.comment: This project is a specific instance of a floating offshore wind project.
http://example.org/BLOW.aristotelian_definition: A project focused on developing and deploying floating offshore wind technologies, with a start date of January 1, 2023.

http://example.org/ICONIC.comment: This project is a specific instance of a wind energy new turbine materials project.
http://example.org/ICONIC.aristotelian_definition: A project focused on the development and application of new materials for wind turbine components, with a start date of December 1, 2023.

http://example.org/PhyDAWN.comment: This project is a specific instance of a wind energy grid integration project.
http://example.org/PhyDAWN.aristotelian_definition: A project focused on enhancing the integration of wind energy into electrical grids, with a start date of July 1, 2023.

http://example.org/Blades2Build.comment: This project is a specific instance of a blade recycling project.
http://example.org/Blades2Build.aristotelian_definition: A project focused on developing and implementing recycling solutions for wind turbine blades, with a start date of January 1, 2023.

http://example.org/EoLO-HUBs.comment: This project is a specific instance of a recycling and circularity project.
http://example.org/EoLO-HUBs.aristotelian_definition: A project focused on recycling and promoting circular economy principles within the wind energy sector, particularly concerning end-of-life components, with a start date of January 1, 2023.

http://example.org/OCEANBATTERY.comment: This project is a specific instance of a grid integration project.
http://example.org/OCEANBATTERY.aristotelian_definition: A project focused on improving the integration of wind energy into existing power grids, with a start date of July 1, 2023.

http://example.org/CleanS_tack.comment: This project is a specific instance of a grid integration project.
http://example.org/CleanS_tack.aristotelian_definition: A project focused on enhancing the integration of wind energy into electrical grids, with a start date of February 1, 2023.

ex:operatesOnYearlyBasisUpTo.comment: Specifies the yearly operational time horizon of the POLES-JRC model.

ex:isUpdatedYearlyWith.comment: Indicates that the POLES-JRC model is updated yearly with specific types of information.

ex:learningRate.comment: Quantifies the percentage change of the cost of an energy technology based on a doubling of its cumulative capacity or production.

ex:floorCost.comment: Specifies the minimum achievable investment cost for a component or technology, acting as a limit for cost reduction through learning.

ex:hasEUFinancialContribution.comment: The EU financial contribution in EUR for a Horizon Europe funded R&I project.

ex:hasResearchArea.comment: The research area or focus of a Horizon Europe funded R&I project.

ex:differsFromScenario.comment: Indicates how this scenario differs from another energy system scenario, particularly in terms of model version, parameter updates, or driving logic.

ex:drivenBy.comment: Describes the primary driver or logic behind an energy system scenario, such as a global carbon price or alignment with climate laws.

ex:considersPolicy.comment: Specifies the climate policies or legislative packages considered within an energy system scenario.
